messages.author: 22e1358c377352d2
messages.subject: Cross type for DH population
parts:
Hello Karl,

I have a question regarding Bi-parental QTL mapping. In my genotype data, three parents are involved, e.g., X, Y, Z. All my materials are inbred lines and double-haploids. So, the individuals I have are either X*Y or X*Z. My genotype data is A, B, H translated. So, A= Homozygous for parent A(AA), B= Homozygous for parent B(BB), H=Heterozygous(AB).X was always considered to be as parent A and Y/Z was considered as parent B while doing the ABH translation.


I am confused, which cross type should I use in RQtl? If I use “cross-type =DH” it shows warning messages as three genotypes are involved. Should I replace all H with missing values so that R can read it as DH or is it ok if I use “F2” as cross-type(which comes by default in “read. cross” function if I don´t specify the cross type?


Thank you very much. Any suggestion would be highly appreciated.


Regards

Ishrat

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Cross type for DH population
parts:
As I understand it, you have two different crosses, X x Y and X x Z, but that you’re pooling them. But what sort of crosses were they? If they are doubled haploid populations, there shouldn’t be any H genotypes at all. Whether to use “dh” or “f2” depends on the nature of the cross that produced the individuals you’re considering.

karl

messages.author: 22e1358c377352d2
messages.subject: Re: Cross type for DH population
parts:
Hello Karl,
Thanks for your kind reply. Actually, I am using secondary data from a commercial pre-breeding program. It is not unusual for commercial pre-breeding to have some level of heterozygosity in the DH lines (which my populations were) due to the methodology of production and growing those DH lines. In practice, unless every spike (which was not done) is bagged the high amount of sterility allows for outcrossing and therefore the chance of heterozygosity is increased. That´s why I got very few H also in my genotype data. I have decided to consider all "H" as missing values and then to use cross-type as "DH".And I have asked for the information regarding the nature of the cross that produced the individuals but haven´t got any reply yet.

Thank you. I hope I am on the right track and any kind of suggestion would be valuable for me.

Regards
Ishrat
